Review queue — harvest ID-2010-2015

55 candidate events, generated 2026-11-17. Decide each one, export the decisions file, apply it with python -m pipeline.queue decide decisions-ID-2010-2015.json on this branch, and push. A move is a year-on-year intensification: form a new move only if the claimant's behaviour is new, more frequent or wider in scope than the previous year's moves shown beside each candidate; otherwise merge the event into the existing move it belongs to. Each card carries a pre-sort (presorted by claude-code/opus): a suggested decision with its reason, prefilled in the form where no draft exists; it is a suggestion, and the decision is yours.

Indonesia's Permanent Mission to the UN sent note verbale No. 480/POL-703/VII/10 to the UN Secretary-General, responding to China's 7 May 2009 note CML/17/2009 and its map, stating that remote or very small features in the South China Sea do not deserve an EEZ or continental shelf of their own and that the so-called 'nine-dotted-lines map' clearly lacks international legal basis and is tantamount to upsetting UNCLOS 1982, and asked that it be circulated to all UN members.

A formal UN note verbale rejecting the legal basis of China's nine-dash line is a verbal/legal assertion of Indonesia's position; declarative. It is Indonesia's first formal written challenge to the line. The DOALOS listing (HTML) gives the date; the note itself is a scanned PDF (text read by OCR, not machine-checkable). [confidence: high]

new move (novelty) — The UN note verbale denying the nine-dotted line any legal basis is Indonesia's first formal written legal challenge to China's line. The 2009 record shows only rejections of China's protest over one seizure (prev-run candidates ev-8356b4f7df, ev-2d42351825), not a challenge to the claim itself.

2015-11-11 (day) South China Sea / Natuna — not placed (no feature in the gazetteer by that name) suggested: declarative pre-sort: new move (novelty) ev-e8207c1d96

Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs Luhut Panjaitan said on 11 November 2015 that Indonesia could take China to an international court (he said the 'International Criminal Court') if Beijing's nine-dash-line claim, which overlaps Indonesian waters, could not be resolved through dialogue.

Actors: Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs Luhut B. Panjaitan

Source

Indonesia Also May Challenge China's South Sea Claims — VOA (AP), 2015-11-11

"We would like to see a solution on this in the near future through dialogue, or we could bring it to the International Criminal Court," Luhut said.

Source

Indonesia says could also take China to court over South China Sea — IMOA (reproducing AFP/Daily Star), 2015-11-11

Indonesia could take China before an international court if Beijing’s claim to the majority of the South China Sea and part of Indonesian territory is not resolved through dialogue

2015-11-12 (day) South China Sea (nine-dash line) — not placed (no feature in the gazetteer by that name) suggested: declarative pre-sort: continuation of ev-1b7562aeac (a candidate, provisional) ev-47783c4ac1

Foreign Ministry spokesman Arrmanatha Nasir said on 12 November 2015 that Indonesia did not recognise the nine-dash line because it was not in line with international law, and that Indonesia had asked China through diplomatic channels to clarify what it meant by the line but had received no answer.

Actors: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, spokesman Arrmanatha Nasir

Source

Indonesia asks China to clarify South China Sea claims — Asia Times (Reuters), 2015-11-12

“The position of Indonesia is clear at this stage that we do not recognize the nine-dash line because it is not in line with … international law,” Indonesian Foreign Ministry spokesman Armanatha Nasir told reporters.
